evidence/behavior-assessment.md.text:
# Behavioral checks

These are direct author executions of the revised skill, not independent consumer runs. The request and actual output for each case are in `cases/`. I used the supplied snapshots and catalog helper for each case. This check assesses the resulting claims, citations, and routing rather than matching instruction wording.

| Case | Expected observable behavior | Observed result | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| May summary | Identify May, report 12 seats and CSV plus JSON, distinguish planned PDF export, cite May, omit build identifier. | Output satisfies each item. | Pass |
| April to May | Add JSON export, increase 8 to 12 seats, cite April and May for each change, invent no removals or shipped PDF export. | Output satisfies each item. | Pass |
| May to April | Remove JSON export, decrease 12 to 8 seats, follow requested direction, cite both inputs. | Output satisfies each item. It also mentions unchanged CSV as context for the removed format. | Pass with a minor instruction mismatch |
| May to May | Report no change, cite the baseline and target, invent no additions or removals. | Output satisfies each item. | Pass |

The reverse output's CSV context conflicts with the instruction to omit unchanged facts. The core facts remain correct. I retained the actual output and did not rewrite the package to fit this minor author deviation.

No missing-field case, changed planned-feature case, missing-helper execution, ambiguous-direction interaction, or independent consumer behavior was tested. Static reading confirms corresponding instructions only where present. No claim of complete workflow coverage follows from these cases. The parent will run an independent blinded consumer test separately.

evidence/check-package.py.text:
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import re
import yaml

root = Path('/tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016')
package = root / 'output/release-notes'
original = root / 'input/release-notes'
before = yaml.safe_load((original / 'SKILL.md').read_text().split('---')[1])
after = yaml.safe_load((package / 'SKILL.md').read_text().split('---')[1])
assert after['name'] == before['name'] == 'release-notes'
assert after['metadata'] == before['metadata'] == {'owner': 'docs'}
assert (package / 'references/summary.md').read_bytes() == (original / 'references/summary.md').read_bytes()
links = re.findall(r'\]\(([^)]+)\)', (package / 'SKILL.md').read_text())
assert len(links) == 2
for link in links:
    resolved = (package / link).resolve()
    assert resolved.is_file(), resolved
    print('Read packaged reference:', resolved)
    print(resolved.read_text())
catalog = json.loads((root / 'catalog.json').read_text())
helper = Path(catalog['release-facts'])
assert helper.is_file()
assert helper.parent.parent != package.parent
assert yaml.safe_load(helper.read_text().split('---')[1])['name'] == 'release-facts'
print('Read catalog helper:', helper)
print(helper.read_text())
source_hashes = json.loads((root / 'evidence/source-hashes-before.json').read_text())
for path, digest in source_hashes.items():
    assert hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest, path
print('PASS name, metadata, unchanged summary, packaged references, catalog helper, unchanged source hashes')

evidence/execution.md.text:
# Execution record

This was a bounded authoring test. Reading juan-mode did not activate persistent mode. Only `output/` and `evidence/` under `/tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016` were written. The input request and caller note controlled delivery. No network call, publication, installation, schedule change, or child dispatch occurred.

The authoring dependency was the catalog entry `skill-creator`, resolved to `/home/ubuntu/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md`. I read that whole file and used its validator. I did not substitute either skill-creator under `/home/ubuntu/.agents/skills/`. The separately installed `release-facts` resolved to `/tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/helper-store/release-facts/SKILL.md` through the supplied JSON catalog.

Jstack leaves resolved through the explicit `/home/ubuntu/Dev/skills/skills/jstack` authoring root. I read `jstack-how`, `jstack-technical-writing`, `jstack-principle-encode-lessons-in-structure`, `jstack-principle-prove-it-works`, and `jstack-principle-test-behavior-not-implementation`. I also read `jstack-setup/references/investigation.md` to check the required jstack-how contract. The source remote was `https://github.com/juancamiloqhz/skills.git`. Absolute paths and hashes are recorded in `source-hashes-before.json`. Unslop resolved through the explicit `/home/ubuntu/.agents/skills/unslop/SKILL.md` path.

The exact playbook is retained in `playbook.md`. Its four numbered steps were copied verbatim into the host task list before task-specific work. Step 1 completed after the dependency read and package revision. Step 2 completed after frontmatter, metadata, packaged reference, and catalog helper checks. Step 3 completed as a bounded author-run test with remaining coverage limits. Step 4 was skipped because publication is prohibited. Opening a PR is unavailable in the mode package and did not run.

The mode's jstack-how procedure did not run because its required child would violate the no-delegation scope. It remains incomplete. The unavailable Feature throughput checkpoint was not invented. The parent owns the separate blinded consumer and pinned upstream source comparison. No claim of complete mode execution is made.

I read source and dependencies with `cat` and `sed`, discovered input files with `rg --files /tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016`, and checked repository identity with `git remote -v`. I used `mkdir -p` to create only the allowed output and evidence directories. I used `cp` to retain the original package and unchanged summary reference. I edited with `apply_patch`. The first draft and writing scan are retained under `draft/` and `writing-audit.md`.

The initial frontmatter validation command was `python3 /home/ubuntu/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py /tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/output/release-notes`. It returned exit code 0 and `Skill is valid!`. I repeated that exact validator with stdout redirected to `evidence/quick-validate.stdout` to retain its output.

The initial reference and metadata check ran as a Python heredoc. `check-package.py` retains the same checks and adds verification of source hashes. It was rerun with stdout retained in `check-package.stdout`. This script checks actual file relationships and preservation. It does not claim to execute natural-language instructions.

I ran `diff -ru /tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/input/release-notes /tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/output/release-notes` before adding validation notes. Exit code 1 meant expected differences. The diff showed the description change, comparison route, explicit catalog resolution, and new comparison reference. No summary difference appeared. The final diff is retained in `package.diff`.

The four behavioral requests and my actual responses are retained in `cases/`. I assessed their facts against the raw snapshots and recorded the result and a minor reverse-case instruction mismatch in `behavior-assessment.md`. These are author-run outputs rather than independent model invocations.

evidence/playbook.md.text:
### Authoring or modifying a skill

**You own the skill's voice.**

1. Use the host's advertised skill-authoring skill, such as **skill-creator**, in place of Cursor's built-in **create-skill**. Read its discovered entrypoint; an absent or inaccessible authoring dependency leaves this step incomplete.
2. Validate the skill: frontmatter has `name` and `description`, referenced files exist, cross-skill links resolve. Resolve packaged files from the skill's own location and independent helpers through the host catalog; do not assume separately installed skills are siblings. Frontmatter validation alone does not establish working references or behavior.
3. Test cases if structural. Skip if subjective.
4. Run **Opening a PR** when publication is authorized. That procedure remains unavailable in this package; disclose the gap rather than claiming it ran. Preserve the requested delivery boundary, including local-only drafts. Authoring does not authorize merging or installation.

When in doubt, delete. Keep only prose that changes a decision. Tell it to do the thing and skip the reason. Explain only when the rule is confusing without one. Match tone to scope. Point at structural sources (types, READMEs, config) per the **jstack-principle-encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill. Delegate to other skills by path. Don't restate. A workflow you keep hitting but isn't captured → propose a new skill.

**Reply:** summary of the skill, key design decisions, validation notes.

evidence/writing-audit.md.text:
# Writing audit

I applied unslop from `/home/ubuntu/.agents/skills/unslop/SKILL.md` and the advertised Codex system skill-creator. The initial authored files are retained in `draft/`. The unmodified starting package is retained in `original/release-notes/`.

The scan found indirect wording in the comparison guidance. "Establish which snapshot is the baseline and which is the target" became "Identify the baseline and target snapshots". "An item absent from a complete list can establish a removal. A missing field cannot." became two direct instructions that name the different evidence states. I added "Report unknown values separately" because the draft's no-change sentence could hide uncertainty.

The self-audit asked what makes the draft obviously AI generated. The repeated use of "establish" and the indirect negative sentence made the instructions harder to follow. I replaced them with commands. The final text keeps the supplied skill's short style and retains the summary guidance byte for byte. No decorative headings, generic conclusion, invented metaphor, or long dash remains in the new package instructions.

Technical-writing mode is how-to for the skill instructions and reference for validation records. I did not find a new abstract metaphor offender to propose to unslop. No unslop edit was made.

output/release-notes/validation.md.text:
# Validation notes

The package adds a comparison route and keeps the summary guidance unchanged. The description now advertises both tasks. Existing `metadata.owner: docs` is preserved. Comparison guidance reports customer-visible additions, removals, and changed limits with citations to both snapshots. The installed release-facts helper still owns fact checking and resolves through the host catalog.

The Codex system skill-creator at `/home/ubuntu/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md` supplied the authoring instructions. Its `scripts/quick_validate.py` completed with exit code 0 and printed `Skill is valid!`. A separate check read both packaged references and the external helper through `/tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/catalog.json`. Name, metadata, and unchanged summary checks passed.

Four author-run cases exercised May summary, April-to-May comparison, reverse comparison, and identical-input comparison. The outputs preserved customer-visible facts and citations. The reverse case mentioned unchanged CSV as context, despite the instruction to omit unchanged facts. The actual outputs remain under `/tmp/jstack-authoring-20261016/evidence/cases`. These author checks do not establish independent consumer behavior or complete workflow coverage.

Publication was prohibited. Opening a PR was skipped and its procedure remains unavailable in the tested jstack package. No publication or installation occurred. The mode's delegated jstack-how procedure remains incomplete because the test prohibits further delegation. The Feature throughput checkpoint procedure is unavailable and was not invented. The parent owns the separate blinded consumer test and pinned upstream comparison.

Prove It Works led to checking the actual output files and helper path. Test Behavior, Not Implementation led to executing comparison and summary requests instead of treating wording checks as behavioral proof. Encode Lessons in Structure led to retaining one shared fact-checking helper and using the host catalog as its source of location.
